tpi_21km.sign_convention: TPI = z - mean(z within the window). TPI < 0 means the cell is LOWER than its surroundings, i.e. INSIDE A BOWL (crater floor, basin, valley). TPI > 0 means a rim, ridge or peak.

roughness_scaling_exponent.fit: OLS of log(sigma) on CENTRED log(achieved scale)
roughness_scaling_exponent.estimator_note: Moving-window standard deviation at four scales, NOT Shepard's deviogram. The name is roughness_scaling_exponent rather than 'hurst' for exactly that reason: the estimator differs from the one the Hurst literature assumes, so these numbers are not interchangeable with published H values.
roughness_scaling_exponent.validated_on: synthetic fractional Brownian surfaces at H = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 using this body's achieved scales; see the fBm gate in the Phase 2 report
roughness_scaling_exponent.outside_unit_interval: Values below 0 and above 1 are NOT errors. This is the slope of log roughness against log scale, which may legitimately exceed 1: it does so where a widening window swallows a discrete feature such as a crater rim and roughness grows faster than linearly. Those pixels are detecting DISCRETE FEATURES rather than fractal texture -- a real measurement of the wrong quantity. A value below 0 says roughness FALLS as the window widens. R2 does not screen either case out, because the power law is clean; only its exponent is meaningless as a texture descriptor. This is also why the layer is named roughness_scaling_exponent and not hurst.
roughness_scaling_exponent.redundancy_finding: VARIABLES.md section B8 predicted HIGH redundancy against ruggedness. That prediction is WRONG. Measured correlation of this layer with roughness_21km on the Moon is -0.157 globally and -0.306 over 85-90S. H carries information nothing else carries; it is simply noisy. The B8 verdict of HOLD stands, but for the signal-to-noise reason, not the redundancy reason.
roughness_scaling_exponent.status: HOLD -- built and stored, not wired into the default dimension set
